Below is a 12-week, upper-body strength program tailored for a recreational climber with right subacromial impingement, cleared for pain-free range only and no overhead loading. It uses a conservative, shoulder-friendly progression, prioritizes scapular control, posterior-chain balance, and graded pulling/pressing in safe ranges. It assumes access to a full gym and coordination with her physio. Stop any movement that provokes pain above 2–3/10 or causes lingering soreness beyond 24–36 hours; reduce load/range as needed.

Structure overview
- Frequency: 3 upper-body sessions/week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri), plus optional low-intensity shoulder care/blood flow on 1–2 nonconsecutive days.
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Tissue capacity, motor control, scapular mechanics, isometrics, and pain-free range strength.
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Hypertrophy/strength-endurance in supported ranges; progress pulling; introduce partial-range pressing below shoulder height; controlled eccentrics.
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Strength emphasis with submaximal loading; climb-specific pulling patterns (horizontal and low-angle vertical), unstable-to-stable shifts; unilateral integration.
  - Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Consolidation and power-endurance touches within safe ranges; graded return-to-climb loading patterns without overhead.

General guardrails
- No overhead loading. Pressing limited to angles that keep humerus below ~80–90° abduction/flexion and are pain-free.
- Favor neutral or supinated grips; avoid provocative wide pronation.
- Emphasize scapular upward rotation control without loading overhead: drills for posterior tilt, depression, and protraction/retraction.
- Tempo: prioritize slow eccentrics (3–4 s) early; move to controlled (2–3 s) mid-phase; introduce moderate intent in concentrics late.
- Progression: add load 2.5–5% or 1–2 reps week-to-week if all sets are RPE 6–7 and pain ≤2/10 during and after. Otherwise hold or regress.
- Climber-specific balance: 2–3× pulling volume relative to pressing, with lots of lower trap, rhomboid, rotator cuff, and posterior delts; isometric grip and forearm endurance without aggravating the shoulder.

Session template (each session)
1) Warm-up (8–10 min): 
   - 3–5 min light cardio
   - Thoracic mobility: segmental cat-cow x8, open books x6/side
   - Scap prep: scapular clocks on wall x6/dir/side, banded scapular retraction with depression x12, gentle serratus wall slides within pain-free range (limit to <90°) x10
2) Main strength A (compound pull)
3) Main strength B (press within allowed range)
4) Accessory row/face pull variant
5) Rotator cuff/scap stabilizers
6) Climber-specific grip/forearm (pain-free)
7) Cooldown: breathing, pec minor doorway stretch (low angle), posterior capsule cross-body stretch, soft-tissue as tolerated

Phase 1: Weeks 1–3 (Restore mechanics, isometrics, base capacity)
Weekly schedule example: 3 sessions (A/B/A then B/A/B alternating weekly)

Week 1
- A1: Chest-supported neutral-grip row (machine or incline bench) 3×12, 3030 tempo, RPE 6
- B1: Push-up to elevated surface (hands on bench), elbows ~30–45°, pain-free depth 3×8–10, 3010, RPE 6
- A2: Half-kneeling cable row ( ipsilateral knee down), focus scap depression/retraction 3×12/side, 3031
- B2: Cable fly low-to-mid (set pulleys just below shoulder height; limit ROM) 2×12, light, 3020
- C1: Prone Y (short range, thumbs up, to 80–90° max) 2×10, 2020
- C2: Side-lying ER (right and left) 3×12, 2020
- C3: Serratus punches (supine with light DB or cable) 3×12
- D: Farmer carry, neutral shoulders, light–moderate 3×30–40 m
- Forearm: Wrist flex/ext isometrics against band 3×20–30 s each; pronation/supination with hammer 2×12 light

Weekly notes and progression
- Add load in small steps if form is crisp, scap control maintained, and shoulder is symptom-stable. If symptoms rise, first reduce ROM, then tempo, then load.

- Keep pressing volume modest; prioritize neutral grips and ROM stops (floor, boards, or safety pins).

Climbing integration (non-overhead, symptom-limited)
- Weeks 1–3: Technique-only footwork drills, slab traverses with feet priority, easy boulders/routes where hands stay below shoulder height; avoid dynamic moves and gastons.

- Weeks 7–9: Build to moderate routes focusing on smooth pulling below shoulder height, controlled movement, 45–60 min.
- Weeks 10–12: Maintain moderate volume; avoid pumpy overhead sequences. Prioritize quality movement.

Recovery, mobility, and monitoring
- Daily (5–8 min): 
  - Posterior capsule cross-body stretch 2×30–45 s
  - Pec minor doorway stretch at low angle 2×30–45 s
  - Thoracic extension over foam roller 6–8 slow reps
  - Scapular CARs: slow circles 5 each direction
- Post-session: 5 min nasal breathing in supine, light soft-tissue to pec minor/infraspinatus as tolerated.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours; side-lying with small pillow supporting upper arm to keep shoulder slightly abducted.
- Pain rule: ≤2–3/10 during; no increase the next day. If exceeded, scale back 10–20% load/ROM and add an extra recovery day.

Optional nutrition notes for strength and tissue support
- Protein: ~1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, 3–4 feedings, include leucine-rich sources.
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day.
- Omega-3 (if appropriate): ~1–2 g EPA+DHA/day may support joint comfort.
- Hydration and carbohydrate around training (20–40 g pre) to aid performance.

Red flags and modifications
- Painful arc especially between ~60–120° flexion/abduction: reduce range, change grip to neutral/supinated, or swap exercise.
- Night pain or increasing resting pain: pause pressing work and consult physio.
- If landmine press is provocative at any time, replace with: cable press at low anchor with neutral handle, push-up variations, or isometric chest press against wall.

This plan builds robust scapular control and pulling strength while carefully dosing press work and keeping all movements well below overhead, providing a safe, progressive return to stronger upper-body function for climbing.

Here’s a practical body recomposition plan to pair with the 12-week upper-body program. Goal: lose fat while building/maintaining lean mass, supporting shoulder health and climbing performance.

Key targets
- Calories: small, sustainable deficit (about 250–400 kcal/day below maintenance)
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day (spread over 3–5 meals)
- Carbohydrate: periodized around training to fuel performance
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day (don’t drop too low; supports hormones and satiety)
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day
- Hydration: bodyweight(kg) × 30–35 mL/day, plus 500–750 mL per training hour

Estimating calories
1) Find maintenance: bodyweight(kg) × 30–33 = baseline kcal. Add 200–400 kcal for very active days; subtract 200–300 kcal for rest days. Or use a tracker (7–10 days) to refine.
2) Create a deficit: start −300 kcal/day average. Expect ~0.3–0.6% bodyweight loss per week while getting stronger.

Macro setup example (adjust to body size)
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day
- Carbs: remainder of calories, with more on training/climbing days and less on rest days
- Training days: aim for 3–5 g/kg carbs (if high climbing volume) or 2.5–3.5 g/kg (moderate)
- Rest days: 1.5–2.5 g/kg carbs

Timing and peri-workout fueling
- Pre-training (60–90 min): 20–40 g carbs + 20–30 g protein; low fat/fiber to avoid GI upset
- During (if sessions >75–90 min or climbing volume high): 20–30 g carbs/hour + electrolytes
- Post-training (within 2 h): 0.3 g/kg protein + 0.5–1.0 g/kg carbs; include some sodium and fluids

Protein distribution
- 3–5 feedings/day with 0.3–0.4 g/kg high-quality protein per meal (20–40 g for most), including:
  - Eggs, poultry, fish, lean red meat, Greek yogurt/skyr, cottage cheese, tofu/tempeh, edamame, whey/plant blends
- Add 1 serving of casein-rich protein (e.g., Greek yogurt/cottage cheese or casein shake) in the evening to support overnight recovery

Carb quality and periodization
- Prioritize: oats, rice, potatoes, pasta, quinoa, whole-grain breads, fruit, low-fat dairy, legumes (tolerance permitting)
- Place larger carb portions around workouts and climbing; scale portions down at dinner on rest days

Fat sources
- Emphasize mono- and polyunsaturated fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, fatty fish
- Keep saturated fat moderate

Micronutrients for shoulder health and performance
- Calcium: 1,000 mg/day and Vitamin D: 1,000–2,000 IU/day (check bloods if possible)
- Magnesium: 300–400 mg/day (glycinate/citrate) if intake is low
- Omega-3s: 1–2 g/day EPA+DHA (or 2–3 servings fatty fish/week)
- Nitrates (beetroot, leafy greens) on heavy training days may aid performance
- Color rule: 2+ cups veggies and 1–2 servings fruit daily

Supplements (optional, evidence-based)
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day, any time
- Whey or plant protein isolate: convenient to hit targets
- Collagen or gelatin (optional for tendons/capsule comfort): 10–15 g with 50–100 mg Vitamin C, 30–60 min before rehab/shoulder work
- Caffeine: 1–3 mg/kg pre-training if tolerated; avoid late-day use if it disrupts sleep
- Note: clear any new supplement with her physician if she has medical conditions

Sample day (training)
- Breakfast: Greek yogurt bowl (250 g) with berries, honey, 30 g granola; 15 g mixed nuts
- Snack (pre-training): whey shake (25–30 g) + banana or fig bar
- Post-training/lunch: rice bowl with 120–150 g chicken or tofu, 1.5 cups rice, mixed veggies, olive oil drizzle
- Snack: cottage cheese (200 g) + pineapple + rice cakes
- Dinner: salmon (140–170 g), roasted potatoes, big salad with olive oil–lemon dressing
- Evening (if protein short): casein shake or skyr

Sample day (rest)
- Breakfast: veggie omelet (3 eggs or tofu), whole-grain toast, avocado
- Lunch: mixed bean and quinoa salad with feta and olive oil
- Snack: skyr + fruit
- Dinner: turkey lettuce wraps or tofu stir-fry with cauliflower rice and edamame
- Optional evening: cottage cheese with cinnamon

Behavioral framework
- 80/20 rule: 80% whole/minimally processed foods; 20% flexible
- Eat slowly, stop at “7/10” fullness; use smaller plates and pre-portion snacks
- Plan protein first at each meal; add veg/fruit; then carbs/fats based on training
- Alcohol: limit to ≤3 drinks/week; avoid around training days

Weekly check-ins and adjustments
- Track: bodyweight (3–4x/week morning average), gym performance (reps/load at RPE), shoulder symptoms, adherence, sleep
- If weight loss >0.7–1.0%/week or energy low: add 100–150 kcal/day (mostly carbs around training)
- If weight stable ≥2 weeks and body comp not improving: subtract 100–150 kcal/day or increase NEAT (extra 3–4k steps/day)
- Performance flag: if lifts stall and recovery declines for >2 weeks, shift to maintenance calories for 7–10 days, then resume mild deficit

Hydration and electrolytes
- Start day with 300–500 mL water + pinch of salt/lemon
- During training: 500–750 mL/hour with 300–600 mg sodium/L if sweating heavily
- Urine pale-straw is a simple target

Special considerations for subacromial impingement
- Avoid rapid weight loss (>1%/week); prioritize protein and creatine to protect lean mass
- Time collagen/gelatin before shoulder-specific sessions if using
- Keep high-fiber/gassy foods away from training if they disrupt bracing or breathing

Deliverables you can share with the client
- Daily protein target: [enter based on her bodyweight] g/day
- Daily fat range: [enter] g/day
- Training-day carbs: [enter] g/day; Rest-day carbs: [enter] g/day
- Total calories: Maintenance ≈ [enter]; Goal ≈ maintenance −300 kcal
- Peri-workout: 20–40 g carbs + 20–30 g protein pre; 0.3 g/kg protein + 0.5–1.0 g/kg carbs post

This plan creates a slight, sustainable deficit while protecting lean mass and strength, supporting recovery of the shoulder, and fueling high-quality training and climbing. Adjust portions weekly based on progress and symptom stability.

Below is a 2x/week cardio plan layered onto the 12-week program to build aerobic base, shoulder-friendly stamina, and climb-day durability without violating “pain-free range only” and “no overhead loading.” It prioritizes long, easy Zone 2 and a progressive mixed-terrain hike/step session to mimic long climbing approaches and on-the-wall endurance.

Guiding principles
- Frequency: 2 sessions/week on nonconsecutive days (e.g., Tue and Sat) away from the hardest upper-body lift day.
- Intensity distribution: ~80–90% easy aerobic (Zone 2), 10–20% controlled tempo/threshold touches later.
- Shoulder rules: no overhead arm carriage; keep hands neutral/relaxed; avoid arm swing if provocative; use chest strap HR if wrist swing bothers shoulder.
- RPE/HR: 
  - Zone 2 = conversational pace, RPE 4–6/10, ~60–70% HRmax or 70–80% HR at VT1.
  - Tempo = “comfortably hard,” RPE 7–8/10, ~80–88% HRmax; only added after Week 6 if symptom-free.

Modality options (rotate as desired)
- Incline treadmill hiking or outdoor hiking (primary)
- Stair machine/StepMill (hands light on rails, neutral shoulders)
- Flat or slight-incline cycling (upright or spin bike)
- Elliptical with fixed handles (do not drive with arms)
- Rowing machine only if pain-free with short stroke and neutral shoulder; otherwise skip early
- Circuit walk: brisk walk with loaded carry intervals (light farmer’s carry) if tolerated

12-week progression
- Session 1 each week = Long Zone 2
- Session 2 each week = Climb-specific stamina (steps/hike) with light muscular endurance elements

Weeks 1–3 (Build base and tolerance)
- Session 1: Long Zone 2
  - Week 1: 35–45 min Zone 2, flat walk or easy bike
  - Week 2: 40–50 min Zone 2
  - Week 3: 45–55 min Zone 2
- Session 2: Incline hike or StepMill
  - Week 1: 25–30 min total. 5-min flat warm-up, then 4×3-min incline (4–7% or StepMill L3–5) with 2-min easy between; 5-min cool-down
  - Week 2: 30–35 min total. 5-min warm-up, 5×3-min incline with 90-s easy; cool-down
  - Week 3: 35–40 min total. 6×3-min incline with 90-s easy

Weeks 4–6 (Extend duration; introduce mild tempo if symptoms stable)
- Session 1: Long Zone 2
  - Week 4: 55–65 min Zone 2
  - Week 5: 60–70 min Zone 2
  - Week 6: 65–75 min Zone 2
- Session 2: Climb-specific stamina
  - Week 4: 40–45 min. Continuous incline hike at 4–8% or StepMill L4–6; keep Zone 2
  - Week 5: 45–50 min. Insert 2×6-min “upper Zone 2/low tempo” blocks at a slightly steeper grade with 4-min easy between
  - Week 6: 50–55 min. 3×6-min low-tempo blocks with 4-min easy between (only if pain-free)

Weeks 7–9 (Tempo touches; specific muscular endurance)
- Session 1: Long Zone 2
  - Week 7: 70–80 min Zone 2
  - Week 8: 75–85 min Zone 2
  - Week 9: 80–90 min Zone 2 (split into 2×40–45 min if schedule requires)
- Session 2: Muscular endurance hike/steps
  - Week 7: 50–55 min. 3×8-min tempo (steeper grade) with 4-min easy between
  - Week 8: 55–60 min. 2×10–12 min tempo with 5-min easy between
  - Week 9: 60 min continuous at steady upper Zone 2; finish with 2×5-min tempo surges separated by 3-min easy

Weeks 10–12 (Climb-day simulation and consolidation)
- Session 1: Long Zone 2 with fueling practice
  - Week 10: 85–95 min Zone 2; practice sipping 200–300 mL fluids every 15–20 min + 20–30 g carbs/hour
  - Week 11: 90–105 min Zone 2; include 2×6–8 min tempo midway
  - Week 12: 70–80 min Zone 2 deload; keep all easy
- Session 2: Climb-day simulation
  - Week 10: 75–90 min mixed terrain or StepMill intervals: 3×12-min steady upper Zone 2 with 4-min easy; optional light farmer’s carry finisher 2×60 m if shoulder-friendly
  - Week 11: 90–105 min hike/outdoor approach if possible; gentle descents; poles optional if they don’t provoke shoulder
  - Week 12: 60–70 min easy incline walk; no tempo

Placement with strength sessions
- Example week: 
  - Mon: Upper A
  - Tue: Cardio 1 (Long Zone 2)
  - Wed: Upper B
  - Thu: Off or shoulder care
  - Fri: Upper A
  - Sat: Cardio 2 (Stamina/steps)
  - Sun: Off
- Keep 24 h between high-volume rowing/landmine press days and the hardest cardio session.

Optional field metrics
- MAF/VT1 pace (talk test) on flat route; track distance covered at fixed HR to gauge aerobic efficiency.
- RPE log and symptom score (0–10) for the shoulder each cardio day.
- Step count goal: progress from current baseline + 2–3k/day up to 10–12k/day by Week 8–10, aligned with recovery.

Shoulder and climbing-specific tweaks
- Keep arm swing relaxed; avoid holding rails with shrugged shoulders on StepMill.
- If any arm position above ~80–90° is provocative, choose bike/flat walk instead that day.
- If soreness >24–36 h or pain >3/10, reduce duration by 10–20% the next week.
- Integrate easy technique traversing on climbing days in place of one cardio session as tolerance allows (hands kept below shoulder height).

Fueling for longer cardio
- For sessions ≤60 min: water + electrolytes as needed.
- For 60–90 min: 20–30 g carbs/hour + 300–500 mL fluids/hour.
- For 90–105+ min: 30–45 g carbs/hour + 400–600 mL fluids/hour; include sodium 300–600 mg/L.
- Practice the same snacks you’d use on long climbing days: chews, bananas, fig bars, rice cakes with honey/peanut butter (thin layer), or diluted sports drink.

Progress checkpoints
- Week 4: Able to complete 50–55 min incline/hike without shoulder provocation.
- Week 8: Long Zone 2 at 75–85 min, steady HR and pace; RPE ≤6.
- Week 11: 90–105 min steady aerobic with fueling; minimal next-day fatigue.
- If these aren’t met, hold the week’s targets and progress only when consistent.

This 2x/week plan builds the aerobic base, leg/respiratory stamina, and fueling skills needed for long climbing days while staying within shoulder-safe constraints. Adjust grade, duration, and tempo based on symptoms and overall training load.

Below is a climbing-specific progression you can layer onto the existing 12-week plan, adding hangboard and prep while honoring: pain-free range only, no overhead loading, and the prior strength/cardio schedule. The emphasis is finger, forearm, and scapular capacity without provocative shoulder angles or dynamic moves. Coordinate with her physio; stop any drill if shoulder pain exceeds 2–3/10 or lingers >24–36 hours.

Structure and placement
- Frequency: 1–2 sessions/week, added in Phases 3–4 (Weeks 7–12) once Weeks 1–6 are symptom-stable.
- Duration: 20–35 minutes/session.
- Scheduling:
  - Preferred: after warm-up on an upper-body day before rows/pressing OR as a short standalone session with at least 24 h before/after the hardest pull day.
  - Avoid pairing with the longest cardio day.
- Shoulder-safe rules:
  - Use feet-on assistance and partial bodyweight. Keep scapulae set in gentle depression/protraction without shrugging.
  - Keep humerus angle below ~80–90° flexion/abduction; hands roughly chest-to-shoulder height. No overhead reach or lock-offs.
  - No explosive campusing/dynos/gastons. Strict, static holds only.
- Warm-up for each session (8–10 min):
  - 3–5 min easy cardio
  - Wrist/finger prep: forearm massage, finger flicks x20, prayer stretch 2×20 s
  - Scap/shoulder: banded scap dep/retraction x12, serratus wall slides to <90° x8–10
  - Movement prep: easy traverse or foot-on hangs at very light load

Progression overview
- Weeks 7–8: Introduce foot-assisted hangs and easy grip density; no max efforts.
- Weeks 9–10: Progress density and slight intensity; add controlled repeaters with generous rest.
- Weeks 11–12: Consolidate with mild capacity increases; brief positional isometrics mimicking low-angle lock-offs (below shoulder height only). Deload volume in Week 12.

Grip selection and holds
- Prioritize: large jug, 20–30 mm edge, sloper; half-crimp only if pain-free, no full crimp.
- Neutral or slightly supinated wrist; avoid extreme pronation if it provokes symptoms.
- Choose a hangboard with big jugs/edges, or use a bar/rings at chest height with feet assistance.

Session details

Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9)
- Week 7 (1x session)
  - Objective: Familiarization, tissue tolerance
  - Setup: Hangboard at reachable height with feet on a box/bench to unload 40–60% bodyweight. Use a pulley system or resistance band for assistance if available.
  - Block A: Foot-on jug isometrics 6×10 s holds, 50–60% BW, rest 50–60 s
  - Block B: Foot-on 25–30 mm edge isometrics 4×8–10 s, 40–50% BW, rest 60–75 s
  - Block C: Scap mechanics on low bar/rings: scapular protract/relax cycles 2×10, then 2×20–30 s assisted “scap hangs” without shoulder elevation
  - Finisher: Forearm recovery pump—very easy rice bucket open/close 2×45 s

- Week 8 (1–2x sessions, 72+ h apart)
  - Block A: Foot-on jug repeaters 5 rounds of 7 s on / 3 s off × 4 reps, rest 90 s between rounds; 50–60% BW
  - Block B: Foot-on 25 mm edge repeaters 4 rounds of 7 s on / 3 s off × 3 reps, rest 2 min; 40–50% BW
  - Block C: Sloper isometrics 3×12 s at easy RPE 6, rest 60–75 s
  - Optional: Low-angle wall traverse (hands below shoulder height), 2×3–4 min continuous, easy pace

- Week 9 (2x sessions if tolerated)
  - Block A: Density repeaters on jug: 7 s on / 3 s off × 5 reps × 4 rounds, 50–60% BW; rest 90 s between rounds
  - Block B: 25 mm edge: 10 s holds × 4 sets at 45–55% BW, rest 75–90 s
  - Block C: Half-crimp technique (only if fully symptom-free): 6–8 s holds × 3 sets on 25–30 mm edge with heavier foot assist; rest 60–75 s
  - Movement integration: Traversing 2×5 min, easy, no overhead or big cross-throughs

Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12)
- Week 10 (2x sessions)
  - Objective: Capacity and mild strength bias without maxing
  - Block A: Jug repeaters: 7/3 × 6 reps × 4 rounds, 50–60% BW; rest 90 s
  - Block B: 20–25 mm edge pyramid:
    - 8 s hold (light assist), rest 60 s
    - 10 s hold (same), rest 75 s
    - 8 s hold, rest 60 s
    - Repeat pyramid twice
  - Block C: Low-angle “micro-lock” isometrics: with feet on, elbow flexion 30–60°, hand at or below shoulder height. Hold 5–6 s × 4/side, rest 45–60 s. Focus scap depression/pack; zero pain.

- Week 11 (1–2x sessions; keep symptom check strict)
  - Block A: Mixed-edge repeaters: alternate jug and 25 mm
    - Round 1: Jug 7/3 × 6
    - Round 2: 25 mm 7/3 × 4
    - Round 3: Jug 7/3 × 6
    - Round 4: 25 mm 7/3 × 4
    - Maintain 45–60% BW with feet assist throughout; rest 90 s between rounds
  - Block B: Sloper endurance: 4×15 s holds at easy–moderate effort, rest 75 s
  - Movement integration: Traverse 2×6–7 min continuous, easy to moderate; strict technique, quiet feet

- Week 12 (Deload; 1x session)
  - Reduce total sets/rounds by ~40–50%; keep assistance the same or increase it
  - Example:
    - Jug repeaters: 7/3 × 5 reps × 2 rounds
    - 25 mm edge: 8–10 s × 2–3 sets
    - Optional 5–6 min easy traverse
  - No micro-locks this week; give tissues a break

Load management and progression rules
- RPE target: 6–7/10 on holds; never to failure; form and shoulder comfort trump load.
- If all sets feel ≤RPE 6 and symptoms are 0–1/10 during and next day, reduce foot assistance slightly next session (i.e., increase effective load by ~5–10%).
- If symptoms rise or form degrades, increase assistance, choose bigger holds, or swap to slopers/jugs only.
- Total weekly time under tension (TUT) target:
  - Week 7: 80–120 s
  - Week 8: 120–180 s
  - Week 9–10: 180–240 s
  - Week 11: 200–260 s
  - Week 12: 100–140 s (deload)

Technique cues
- “Long neck” with gentle scapular depression; avoid shrugging or anterior tilt.
- Elbows stay slightly in front of torso, not flared wide.
- Neutral wrist; avoid aggressive ulnar deviation.
- Feet carry as much load as needed to keep shoulder quiet and movement smooth.

Integration with the existing plan
- Option A (preferred on strength days):
  - Warm-up
  - Hangboard block (15–20 min)
  - Main lifts (rows/presses)
  - Accessories/cuff
  - This preserves finger quality while keeping overall session length reasonable.
- Option B (standalone):
  - Short hangboard + easy traverse on a day before Long Zone 2 cardio or on the lighter lifting day. Keep the total ≤30 min.

Forearm and connective tissue support
- Continue rice bucket, finger extension bands 2–3x/week.
- Collagen/gelatin 10–15 g + 50–100 mg vitamin C, 30–60 min before hangboard/shoulder work (optional).

- Session 1: W4 55–65 min; W5 60–70; W6 65–75 (Zone 2)
- Session 2: W4 40–45 min continuous incline; W5 add 2×6-min low-tempo; W6 3×6-min low-tempo (only if shoulder ok)

Saturday Finisher
- Keep 25–30 min; add one round or slight load if symptom-free.

Phase 3: Weeks 7–11 (Intensity push to peak)
Strength shifts to higher intensity per our update. Hangboard starts here. Cardio maintains base with selective tempo.

Week 7
- Upper A
  - A1 Chest-supported row 4–5×5, RPE 8, 21X1; optional +set leaving 2 RIR
  - A2 One-arm cable row (diagonal) 3×6–8/side, RPE 8
  - B1 Floor press (neutral) 4×6, RPE 7.5–8
  - C1 Face pull to ER 3×10–12
  - C2 ER 30–45° 3×10–12
  - D Farmer carry heavy 4×30–40 m, RPE 8
- Upper B
  - A1 Seal row or heavy machine row 5×4–6, RPE 8–8.5
  - A2 Neutral-grip pulldown (to chin/upper chest) 3×6–8, RPE 8
  - B1 Landmine press single-arm 4×5–6, RPE 7.5–8
  - C1 Reverse fly 3×10–12
  - C2 Serratus punches 3×12–15
  - D Bottoms-up KB carry at side 3×15–20 m/side
- Upper C
  - A1 One-arm chest-supported row 5×3–5/side, RPE 8.5–9
  - B1 Floor press 5×3–5, RPE 8
  - B2 Cable low–mid fly 2–3×10
  - C1 Face pull 2–3×12
  - C2 ER isometric 30–45° 3×20–30 s
- Hangboard (1x this week, 20–25 min)
  - Jug repeaters 7/3 × 6 × 3–4 rounds, 50–60% BW assist
  - 25–30 mm edge 10 s × 4–5 sets at 40–50% BW assist
  - Sloper holds 12–15 s × 3
- Cardio
  - Long Zone 2: 70–80 min
  - Stamina/steps: 50–55 min with 3×8-min tempo if fresh; otherwise steady
- Saturday Finisher
  - Option 2 EMOM 20 or Option 3; RPE 7.5–8; strict form

Week 8
- Strength: repeat Week 7 loads, aim small increases if clean (same structure)
- Hangboard (1–2x, 72 h apart)
  - Session: Jug repeaters 7/3 × 6 × 3–4 rounds; 25 mm edge 10 s × 4–5 sets; Sloper 12–15 s × 3
- Cardio
  - Long Zone 2: 75–85 min
  - Stamina/steps: 55–60 min; 2×10–12 min tempo if shoulder ok
- Saturday Finisher
  - Option 1 or 2; small load bump or 1 extra rep where safe

Week 9
- Upper A
  - A1 Chest-supported row 6×3–4, RPE 8.5–9
  - A2 One-arm cable row 3×5–6/side, RPE 8–8.5
  - B1 Floor press 5×3–4, RPE 8
  - C1 Face pull to ER 3×10
  - D Farmer carry heavy 4×30 m
- Upper B
  - A1 Seal row or machine row heavy 5×3–4, RPE 8.5–9
  - A2 Neutral pulldown (range-limited) 3×5–6, RPE 8–8.5
  - B1 Landmine press single-arm 5×3–4, RPE 8–8.5
  - C1 Reverse fly 3×10–12
  - C2 ER 45° 3×8–10
- Upper C
  - A1 One-arm chest-supported row 5×2–3/side, RPE 9, pristine form
  - B1 Floor press 4×3, RPE 8
  - B2 Cable fly short ROM 2×8–10
  - Finisher: Row density 30 s on/30 s off × 4–6 min at ~70% of A1 load
- Hangboard (2x)
  - Session 1 (strength bias): 25 mm edge 8–10 s × 5–6 sets at 50–60% BW assist; Jug repeaters 7/3 × 6 × 3 rounds; Micro-lock isos feet-on, elbow 30–60°, 6 s × 4/side
  - Session 2 (capacity bias): Alternating repeaters (Jug 7/3 × 6; rest 60 s; 25 mm 7/3 × 4; rest 90 s; repeat once); Sloper 15 s × 3–4
- Cardio
  - Long Zone 2: 80–90 min
  - Stamina/steps: 60 min steady, optional 2×5-min tempo surges
- Saturday Finisher
  - Option 3 or 4; RPE 7.5–8; cap at 25–30 min

Week 10
- Strength: Same structure as Week 9; aim for tiny load bumps or improved bar speed; keep technique perfect.
- Hangboard (2x, similar to Week 9)
- Cardio
  - Long Zone 2: 85–95 min with fueling practice (20–30 g carbs/h, 300–600 mg Na/L)
  - Stamina/steps: 75 min steady; no excessive tempo if fatigue accumulates
- Saturday Finisher
  - One higher-effort session (RPE ~8) but volume flat

Week 11 (Sharpening; volume −15–20%, intensity maintained)
- Upper A
  - A1 Chest-supported row 4×3, RPE 8.5
  - A2 One-arm cable row 2–3×4–5/side, RPE 8
  - B1 Floor press 3×3–4, RPE 7.5–8
  - C1 Face pull 2×10–12
  - D Farmer carry 3×25–30 m
- Upper B
  - A1 Seal row/machine row 4×3, RPE 8.5
  - A2 Neutral pulldown 2×4–5, RPE 8
  - B1 Landmine press 3×3–4, RPE 7.5–8
  - Light cuff 2×10–12
- Upper C (speed-strength feel)
  - A1 One-arm cable row 5×3/side at ~70% Week 9 load; fast concentric, 2 s ecc
  - B1 Floor press 5×2 at ~70–75% with crisp speed
  - Minimal accessories + mobility
- Hangboard (1–2x, lower volume)
  - Session A: 25 mm edge 8–10 s × 4–5 sets; Jug repeaters 7/3 × 5 × 2 rounds
  - Optional Session B: easy sloper/jug repeaters only, very submax
- Cardio
  - Long Zone 2: 90–105 min with fueling
  - Stamina/steps: 75–90 min steady; NO tempo
- Saturday Finisher
  - Reduce volume 15–20% (shorter EMOM/AMRAP or one fewer round)

Phase 4: Week 12 (Deload/taper and peak for trip)
- Strength (2 short primers early week, 48–72 h before first big climb day)
  - Day 1: Chest-supported row 3×3 RPE 7; Floor press 3×3 RPE 6–7; Face pull + ER 2×10
  - Day 2 (optional): One-arm cable row 3×3/side RPE 7; Landmine press 2–3×3 RPE 6–7; light cuff, mobility
- Hangboard (one light primer 3–4 days pre-trip)
  - Jug repeaters 7/3 × 4 × 2 rounds at high assistance (easy)
  - 25 mm edge 6–8 s × 2–3 sets at RPE 5–6
- Cardio
  - One easy 60–70 min Zone 2 early week; later in week do only light walking
- Saturday Finisher
  - Skip within 48–72 h of big climb days. If desired early week, do a very light 15–18 min Option 4.
- Mobility
  - Keep daily microdose; emphasize breathing, thoracic, pec/posterior capsule; no aggressive new ranges.

Nutrition plan (body recomposition)
- Calories: mild deficit on most days (−300 kcal from maintenance); push to maintenance on the heaviest training/hangboard weeks (Weeks 9–11) and on climb days in Week 12.
- Maintenance estimate: BW(kg) × 30–33 kcal; refine via 7–10 days tracking.
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day, split 3–5 meals; 0.3–0.4 g/kg per meal.
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day.
- Carbs: fill remainder; periodize more on training days (2.5–3.5 g/kg; up to 3–5 g/kg with higher climbing volume), less on rest days (1.5–2.5 g/kg).
- Peri-workout: 20–40 g carbs + 20–30 g protein 60–90 min pre; 0.3 g/kg protein + 0.5–1.0 g/kg carbs within 2 h post; for cardio >75–90 min, 20–30 g carbs/h + electrolytes (Na 300–600 mg/L).
- Supplements (optional): creatine 3–5 g/day; omega-3 (1–2 g EPA+DHA); vitamin D 1000–2000 IU; magnesium 300–400 mg; whey/plant protein; collagen/gelatin 10–15 g + 50–100 mg Vit C 30–60 min pre-shoulder/hangboard.
- Behavior: 80/20 whole foods; slow eating; 7–9 h sleep; limit alcohol ≤3 drinks/week.

Cardio plan (2x/week)
- Session 1: Long Zone 2 progression across phases as listed above (build to 90–105 min by Week 11; deload Week 12).
- Session 2: Incline/steps stamina with tempo blocks introduced Weeks 5–9 only if symptom-free; steady in Week 11; easy in Week 12.
- Fuel long sessions ≥60–75 min as per nutrition.

Saturday Finisher Day (25–35 min, fun full-body; rotate options)
- Option 1 Carry + Row Gauntlet
- Option 2 Low-Box Punk EMOM
- Option 3 Grip & Grit Circuit
- Option 4 Flow AMRAP
- Option 5 Trail Mix outdoor circuit
- Rules: no overhead; RPE 7–8.5; progress modestly; Week 11 reduce 15–20%; Week 12 skip near climb days.

Climbing-specific prep and hangboard (Weeks 7–12)
- Frequency: 1–2x/week, 20–30 min, 72 h apart when 2x.
- Assistance: feet-on/pulley to keep shoulder quiet; hands chest-to-shoulder height; no dynamic moves.
- Weeks 7–8: Jug/edge repeaters at 50–60% and 40–50% BW assist respectively; sloper isos; optional easy traverse below shoulder height.
- Weeks 9–10: Increase density or reduce assistance slightly if symptom-free; add micro-lock isos feet-on (elbow 30–60°).
- Week 11: Volume −20–30%, intensity quality maintained.
- Week 12: One easy primer only.

Recovery and monitoring
- Sleep 7–9 h; side-lying with pillow under upper arm to keep slight abduction.
- Post-session cool-down: 3–5 min nasal breathing; low-angle pec/posterior capsule stretches.
- Symptom log: pain during/after (0–10), next-day stiffness, exercise notes. If pain >3/10 or night/rest pain appears, reduce next session’s load/ROM 10–20%, increase assistance, and consult physio.

Progress checkpoints
- Week 4: Rows/presses progressing with zero flare-ups; incline cardio ≥45 min steady.
- Week 8: 75–85 min Long Zone 2 at RPE ≤6; hangboard repeaters tolerated without next-day shoulder symptoms.
- Week 11: Heavy pulls feel strong with crisp form; long cardio 90–105 min with fueling; overall freshness improving.
- Week 12: Arrive fresh; minimal DOMS; shoulder calm.

This integrated 12-week plan builds robust, shoulder-safe pulling and pressing strength, aerobic durability, finger capacity, and mobility; intensifies smartly in Weeks 7–10; tapers in Week 11; and peaks in Week 12 for her climbing trip. Adjust loads, assistance, and volume weekly based on RPE, performance, and symptom stability.

Below is the complete 12-week program, integrating all adjustments: pain-free range only; no overhead loading; strength with an intensity push in Phase 3; 2x/week cardio; hangboard/climbing-specific prep in later phases; daily mobility; body recomposition nutrition; and a Saturday Finisher Day. Coordinate with her physio. Pain rule: stop any movement if pain >2–3/10 or lingers >24–36 h; regress load/ROM/tempo as needed.

Structure overview
- Weekly schedule example:
  - Mon: Upper A + Mobility
  - Tue: Cardio 1 (Long Zone 2) + Mobility
  - Wed: Upper B + Mobility
  - Thu: Optional Mobility-only or light shoulder care
  - Fri: Upper C + Mobility
  - Sat: Cardio 2 (Incline/Steps) + Saturday Finisher (short) + Mobility
  - Sun: Off + Mobility microdose
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Mechanics, base capacity, isometrics
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Hypertrophy/strength-endurance, controlled eccentrics
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 7–11): Intensity push to peak strength/capacity (includes hangboard build; taper Week 11)
  - Phase 4 (Week 12): Deload/taper and peak for trip
- Global rules:
  - No overhead loading; keep humerus below ~80–90° elevation; favor neutral/supinated grips.
  - Progress load 2.5–5% when RPE ≤7 and symptoms ≤2/10; otherwise hold or regress.
  - Tempo emphasis early (3–4 s ecc), then controlled (2–3 s), then speed on concentric late while keeping ecc controlled.
  - Pull:Press volume ≈ 2–3:1.

Warm-up template for lift days (8–10 min)

Nutrition plan (body recomposition)
- Calories: mild deficit on most days (−300 kcal from maintenance); push to maintenance on the heaviest training/hangboard weeks (Weeks 9–11) and on climb days in Week 12.
- Maintenance estimate: BW(kg) × 30–33 kcal; refine via 7–10 days tracking.
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day, split 3–5 meals; 0.3–0.4 g/kg per meal.
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day.
- Carbs: fill remainder; periodize more on training days (2.5–3.5 g/kg; up to 3–5 g/kg with higher climbing volume), less on rest days (1.5–2.5 g/kg).
- Peri-workout: 20–40 g carbs + 20–30 g protein 60–90 min pre; 0.3 g/kg protein + 0.5–1.0 g/kg carbs within 2 h post; for cardio >75–90 min, 20–30 g carbs/h + electrolytes (Na 300–600 mg/L).
- Supplements (optional): creatine 3–5 g/day; omega-3 (1–2 g EPA+DHA); vitamin D 1000–2000 IU; magnesium 300–400 mg; whey/plant protein; collagen/gelatin 10–15 g + 50–100 mg Vit C 30–60 min pre-shoulder/hangboard.
- Behavior: 80/20 whole foods; slow eating; 7–9 h sleep; limit alcohol ≤3 drinks/week.

Cardio plan (2x/week)
- Session 1: Long Zone 2 progression across phases as listed above (build to 90–105 min by Week 11; deload Week 12).
- Session 2: Incline/steps stamina with tempo blocks introduced Weeks 5–9 only if symptom-free; steady in Week 11; easy in Week 12.
- Fuel long sessions ≥60–75 min as per nutrition.

Climbing-specific prep and hangboard (Weeks 7–12)
- Frequency: 1–2x/week, 20–30 min, 72 h apart when 2x.
- Assistance: feet-on/pulley to keep shoulder quiet; hands chest-to-shoulder height; no dynamic moves.
- Weeks 7–8: Jug/edge repeaters at 50–60% and 40–50% BW assist respectively; sloper isos; optional easy traverse below shoulder height.
- Weeks 9–10: Increase density or reduce assistance slightly if symptom-free; add micro-lock isos feet-on (elbow 30–60°).
- Week 11: Volume −20–30%, intensity quality maintained.
- Week 12: One easy primer only.

Recovery and monitoring
- Sleep 7–9 h; side-lying with pillow under upper arm to keep slight abduction.
- Post-session cool-down: 3–5 min nasal breathing; low-angle pec/posterior capsule stretches.
- Symptom log: pain during/after (0–10), next-day stiffness, exercise notes. If pain >3/10 or night/rest pain appears, reduce next session’s load/ROM 10–20%, increase assistance, and consult physio.

Progress checkpoints
- Week 4: Rows/presses progressing with zero flare-ups; incline cardio ≥45 min steady.
- Week 8: 75–85 min Long Zone 2 at RPE ≤6; hangboard repeaters tolerated without next-day shoulder symptoms.
- Week 11: Heavy pulls feel strong with crisp form; long cardio 90–105 min with fueling; overall freshness improving.
- Week 12: Arrive fresh; minimal DOMS; shoulder calm.

This integrated 12-week plan builds robust, shoulder-safe pulling and pressing strength, aerobic durability, finger capacity, and mobility; intensifies smartly in Weeks 7–10; tapers in Week 11; and peaks in Week 12 for her climbing trip. Adjust loads, assistance, and volume weekly based on RPE, performance, and symptom stability.
